headline: ARRAS MINERALS ELEMES: 935M AT 0.71% CuEq NEAR-SURFACE IN KAZAKHSTAN — PROGRAM DOUBLES TO 40,000M ON $25M RAISE (TSXV:ARK)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Arras Minerals Corp.
snippet: Arras Minerals (TSXV: ARK) announced July 9 that following the close of an upsized C$25 million bought deal, it is expanding its 2026 diamond drilling program at the Elemes copper-gold porphyry in northeastern Kazakhstan from 20,000 to 40,000 metres — alongside drill results from the Berezski North target showing hole EL26032 returning 935.9 metres at 0.71% copper equivalent from near surface, including 214.9 metres at 1.42% CuEq. At the Bozshakol-Chingiz metallogenic belt — the same belt hosting KAZ Minerals' operating Bozshakol copper-gold mine 60 km northwest — a near-surface 935-metre copper equivalent intercept, funded by a freshly closed bought deal and now targeting 40,000 metres of drilling, puts Elemes in the category of porphyry discoveries that attract institutional capital on first-look metrics alone.

headline: WEST POINT GOLD NE TYRO WIDENS AT DEPTH: 56.4M AT 4.24 G/T AU INSIDE 68.2M AT 2.20 G/T — ZONE OPEN DOWN-DIP IN ARIZONA (TSXV:WPG)
snippet: West Point Gold (TSXV: WPG) reported July 9 that hole GC26-168 at the Northeast Tyro zone of the Gold Chain Project in Mohave County, Arizona returned 56.4 metres at 4.24 g/t Au from 242.3 metres depth — including 28.9 metres at 7.77 g/t Au — while GC26-161 added 68.2 metres at 2.20 g/t Au (34.3m at 3.57 g/t), with both holes expanding the zone downward and continuing a pattern in which grade and width increase at depth. On the Walker Lane structural trend, GC26-168's 56.4m at 4.24 g/t Au signals an undepleted high-grade core below the current drill envelope — and the zone remains open, making the next program's scope-defining question whether that core is large enough to support a maiden resource estimate.

headline: ATHA ENERGY'S SIXTH DISCOVERY AT ANGILAK: 11.5M COMPOSITE URANIUM AT LAC 50 NORTHWEST, 4KM ALONG STRIKE FROM DEPOSIT (TSXV:SASK)
source_name: Investing News Network / ATHA Energy Corp.
snippet: ATHA Energy (TSXV: SASK) announced July 8 that the second drillhole at the new Lac 50 Northwest Discovery at the Angilak Uranium Project in Nunavut intersected 11.5 metres of composite uranium mineralization over five zones from 305 to 480 metres depth — including 7.0 metres averaging 7,974 counts per second and a 1.6-metre high-grade core peaking at 40,162 CPS — located 4 kilometres along strike from the known Lac 50 Deposit area. This is the sixth separate regional discovery at Angilak in 15 months; basement-style uranium in brecciated basalts with albite-hematite alteration matches Athabasca Basin deposit templates, and with three rigs running through September on a 20,000-metre program, ATHA's systematic corridor testing is producing discovery-grade intercepts at a rate that should deliver multiple additional results before season-end.

headline: BHP WINS CHILE APPROVAL FOR $14.7B ESCONDIDA EXPANSION — WORLD'S BIGGEST COPPER MINE GETS ENVIRONMENTAL NOD FOR DECADE CAPEX
snippet: Chile's Antofagasta Environmental Assessment Commission approved BHP's plans on July 7 for a first US$1.3 billion tranche of sulfide leaching and electricity upgrades at Escondida — Phase 1 of an estimated US$14.7 billion expansion program aimed at sustaining and growing output at the world's largest copper mine through the 2030s, with BHP targeting nearly double its current global copper production by mid-decade. BHP holds 57.5% of Escondida alongside Rio Tinto (30%) and a Japanese consortium; the clearance unlocks Phase 1 construction, and the sheer scale of total planned capex makes Escondida's expansion the most consequential single copper supply project on the planet — directly relevant context for understanding why junior copper project valuations remain supported even as near-term macro uncertainty weighs on spot prices.

headline: ANDINA COPPER CONFIRMS THIRD PIUQUENES PORPHYRY: 468M AT 0.50% CU, 164M AT 0.70% CU IN FIRST DISCOVERY HOLE, ARGENTINA (TSXV:ANDC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Andina Copper Corp.
snippet: Andina Copper (TSXV: ANDC) confirmed July 8 the discovery of a new copper-gold porphyry at Piuquenes North in San Juan, Argentina — hole PIU13 returning 468 metres at 0.50% Cu, 0.30 g/t Au, and 3.04 g/t Ag from 700 metres, including a 164-metre higher-grade core at 0.70% Cu, 0.44 g/t Au — while PIU12 confirmed lateral extent, together establishing a third porphyry center alongside the previously reported Piuquenes Central and East systems. A multiphase porphyry system intersected over 500 metres of downhole width from 664 to 1,168 metres, with all three porphyry centers in a compact footprint, makes Piuquenes one of the more compelling multi-center copper-gold systems to emerge in South America in the current exploration cycle — and the first drill test at each center has consistently delivered.

headline: ATEX VALERIANO PHASE VI: 20M AT 4.10% CuEq INSIDE 78M AT 3.03% — B2B BRECCIA NOW 600M STRIKE, FINAL 35% OF ASSAYS STILL PENDING
snippet: ATEX Resources (OTCQX: ATXRF) released July 8 additional Phase VI results from the Valeriano Copper-Gold Project in Chile's Atacama — hole ATXD23C returning 124 metres at 2.65% CuEq with a 20-metre core at 4.10% CuEq within 78 metres at 3.03% CuEq at the southern boundary of the High-Grade B2B Breccia, while ATXD31A/31B confirmed northward continuity at up to 408 metres of 0.88% CuEq. Phase VI totalled ~28,400 metres against a 25,000-metre target — a 14% overrun that signals results exceeding expectations — with the B2B breccia now traced over 600 metres of strike (a 50% extension) and 35% of Phase VI assays still pending through July; the remaining results represent the next material catalyst for Valeriano's resource estimate update.

headline: GOLD TO $4,076, SILVER -4%: FED MINUTES SHOW 9-TO-8 SPLIT ON RATE HIKE AND TRUMP KILLS IRAN PEACE DEAL — METALS CAUGHT IN THE CROSSFIRE
snippet: Gold spot fell to US$4,076 per ounce on July 8 as the Federal Reserve's June FOMC minutes revealed a 9-to-8 vote in favour of a 2026 rate hike — with inflation forecasts revised sharply higher and real yields firming — while silver dropped 4.17% to $58.80/oz as President Trump simultaneously declared the interim U.S.-Iran peace agreement over, sending oil prices surging more than 5% and stoking stagflationary concerns. Gold partially recovered to $4,123 on July 9 as geopolitical risk was repriced, leaving precious metals suspended between a structural demand floor (central bank accumulation, Asian buying) and a policy ceiling (rising rate-hike probability); with July 14's CPI print the next key input, the Fed's near-even split makes the next few weeks of U.S. data decisive for whether gold's $4,000–$4,200 range holds or breaks.

headline: TROILUS Z87 ADDS 164M AT 0.95 G/T AuEq — METHODICAL RECORING OF UNSAMPLED RESERVE PIT INTERVALS DELIVERS RESOURCE UPGRADE PATHWAY (TSX:TLG)
snippet: Troilus Mining (TSX: TLG) announced July 7 that hole 87-26-507 at the Z87 optimization program at the Troilus Project in north-central Quebec returned 164 metres at 0.95 g/t AuEq (0.83 g/t Au, 1.30 g/t Ag, 0.06% Cu) — including 46 metres at 1.38 g/t AuEq and 61 metres at 1.22 g/t AuEq — while systematically assaying historically unsampled intervals inside the established Z87 pit shell; 20 holes totalling 5,563 metres complete of an approximately 24,000-metre program. By recoring rather than drilling greenfields, each intercept at these grades converts existing inferred or unclassified material to higher-confidence categories, a lower-risk path to measurable reserve growth that could directly reduce the discount applied to Troilus's resource base in any revised feasibility study at current gold prices.

headline: GOLDGROUP-GOLD RESOURCE MERGER CLEARS BC COURT — $372M MEXICO GOLD-SILVER DEAL CLOSING JULY 17 AFTER FINAL ORDER GRANTED
snippet: The British Columbia Supreme Court granted the final arrangement order for Goldgroup Mining's acquisition of Gold Resource Corporation, clearing the last legal hurdle to close on or about July 17 — following shareholder approval from both companies on July 2. The combined entity becomes a multi-mine, Mexico-focused precious metals producer spanning Goldgroup's Cerro Prieto and San Francisco projects in Sonora and Gold Resource's Don David mine in Oaxaca, along with the Back Forty critical minerals project in Michigan; at $4,100/oz gold and $59/oz silver — materially above the economics cited in pre-merger disclosures — the surviving company's revenue profile arrives on day one of combined operations with a commodity tailwind baked in.

headline: CANADA'S OLDEST DIAMOND MINE ON THE CLOCK — EKATI JULY 28 CCAA SALE DEADLINE APPROACHES AS 74% ROUGH DIAMOND CRASH FORCES RESTRUCTURING
snippet: Arctic Canadian Diamond Company — operator of Canada's Ekati Mine in the Northwest Territories, the country's oldest operating diamond mine — is under CCAA creditor protection granted May 1, 2026, with the British Columbia Supreme Court's stay now extended to July 28 and a court-supervised sale and investment solicitation process underway. A collapse in rough diamond prices from approximately US$92 per carat in late 2024 to as low as US$24/carat by December 2025 — a 74% decline driven by U.S. tariffs on natural diamonds, sustained weak global luxury demand, and rising fuel costs — triggered the insolvency; with the July 28 deadline now less than three weeks away, the next hearing determines whether Ekati passes to new ownership, undergoes financial restructuring, or faces a more serious outcome for its workforce, contractors, and Indigenous community partners.

headline: CHINA SILVER IMPORTS 790+ TONNES EARLY 2026 AS SOLAR DEMAND CEMENTS SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT — INDUSTRIAL FLOOR HOLDS DESPITE RATE PRESSURE | GoldSeek
snippet: VanEck's weekly Gold SWOT column highlights China's silver imports exceeding 790 tonnes in early 2026 — driven principally by solar photovoltaic manufacturing — as structural confirmation that the silver market is on track for its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit, projected at approximately 67 million ounces against total supply growing just 1.5% to a decade-high 1.05 billion ounces. The key tension: Western investment demand for silver remains suppressed by rising U.S. rates and a firming dollar, while industrial consumption from solar and grid buildout in Asia continues to compound; a sixth consecutive deficit with no meaningful supply-side response has historically resolved through price rather than new primary silver supply, given silver's predominantly byproduct mining status.

headline: MINING STOCKS STILL WAITING FOR THE CATALYST THAT CLOSES THE GAP WITH GOLD — THIS WEEK IN MINING, GOLD SEEKER ISSUE #72 | GoldSeek
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold Seeker Issue #72 identifies the current market as a consolidation phase in which the fundamental case for gold mining equities is intact but institutional investors are sidelined awaiting a definitive catalyst — either a Federal Reserve pivot or a geopolitical shock large enough to push safe-haven flows into miners, not just bullion. With GDX's ratio to gold near multi-year lows despite operating margins historically consistent with sector re-rating at $4,000+ gold, the column frames the equity discount as a positioning anomaly rather than a fundamental deterioration, and looks to the H2 2026 data cycle — beginning with July 14's CPI print — as the likely trigger for the rotation that closes miners' lagging gap with the physical metal they leverage.
